sources.versionContext: Archived 2022-12-05 page before pinned February 2023 candidate; does not apply the 7.38 pure-damage changes.
sources.observation: Spell lifesteal is capped by victim remaining HP, has a reduced creep coefficient and excludes Rum repayment and False Promise resolution.

sources.versionContext: Archived 2023-02-15, close to pinned candidate. Modern Oracle barrier ordering is different.
sources.observation: False Promise negates original damage and settles health removal without ordinary multipliers. In this historical model it precedes Aphotic Shield and interacts separately with Borrowed Time.
Rum reduces ordinary incoming damage. Repayment is nonlethal health setting, rather than a new spell damage instance that can lifesteal.

engineRequirements.rule: Negated False Promise damage and its final health-removal settlement do not grant spell lifesteal, while final effective damage keeps original source attribution.

testEvidence.test: False Promise neither the negated original hit nor the final HP removal grants spell lifesteal
False Promise retains damage ownership without reviving an expired provider at settlement

engineRequirements.rule: Rum repayment does not trigger spell lifesteal a second time, and its effective repayment remains attributed to original abilities.

testEvidence.test: AR-E11 does not spell-lifesteal from rum repayment while preserving its original damage attribution

engineRequirements.rule: Historical False Promise must record damage before consuming Aphotic Shield. Current engine still consumes shields first; modern ordering cannot certify this historical combination.
Historical False Promise also records damage when Borrowed Time converts it into deferred healing. Current Borrowed Time early return prevents recording that damage.

Historical generic spell lifesteal uses a 0.2 creep coefficient with source/type exceptions. Engine currently lacks a general native victim-class coefficient; per-illusion and summon inheritance still needs explicit eligibility review.
